summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using " summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Teleport to a far away structure such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Look at the chunks near you; are they loading in?
3a. If the chunks aren’t loading in, reload chunks using `F3 + A`. 
3b. If the chunks still don’t load in, try teleporting closer to the structure.
4a. If the chunks still didn’t load in after the previous steps, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
4b. If the chunks still didn’t load in, ensure you are using the correct version of Minecraft as specified in the original report.
5. To exit if this happens, do NOT use `F3 + C` or `ALT + F4`. 
6. On Windows, open Task Manager and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary".
7. On Linux, open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using `kill <pid>` or use `killall OpenJDK`.
8. On MacOS, press and hold Command + Option + Shift, then press Esc to confirm force quit. 
9. Document that you experienced the server hang and chunks not loading while near a structure with naturally generated allays.
Observed Behavior: The issue occurs when the game becomes unresponsive while attempting to load chunks that contain structures with naturally generated allays. After teleporting several thousand blocks away, players experience a complete halt in chunk loading, even though the F3 menu remains accessible. The internal server tick rate is displayed at 18ms, indicating that the server is still running but unable to process chunk loading. Attempts to reload chunks using the F3 + A command do not resolve the problem, and during the hang, players are unable to execute commands or interact with the game in any meaningful way. Occasionally, a small number of chunks, between two to eight, may load if the player is outside the structure with allays. However, if players try to save their world while chunks are not loading, they encounter a critical issue where the game cannot save, forcing them to crash the game, which results in the loss of any unsaved data. It is important to note that summoning an allay using the command "summon allay" does not trigger this issue, nor does visiting a woodland mansion devoid of naturally generated allays. The problem is isolated to structures that contain naturally generated allays. To reproduce the bug, players should teleport to distant structures such as woodland mansions or pillager outposts, check if the surrounding chunks load, and follow specific steps depending on the response of the chunks. If the chunks do not load after several attempts, the bug has been successfully reproduced. Players must ensure they are using the correct version of the game, specifically 22w13a, as this issue may have been addressed in later snapshots. In case of a hang, standard exit methods like F3 + C or ALT + F4 are ineffective, and players must resort to terminating the game process through their operating system's task manager or equivalent tools.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting to a distant structure containing naturally generated allays, the game should seamlessly load nearby chunks without any interruptions. Players should be able to access the F3 menu and other UI elements, which should function normally, allowing for commands and actions to be executed without delay. Chunks should load consistently, enabling smooth gameplay and allowing players to save their worlds without encountering any freezing or crashing issues.
